newsitem.title: UK: Sterling strength main UK exporter worry - survey.
newsitem.headline: Sterling strength main UK exporter worry - survey.

text.p: The strong pound is still the biggest worry for British exporters both near and long-term, according to a DHL quarterly export indicator survey published on Monday.

Sixty-eight percent of UK exporters said they expected sterling strength to have a negative impact on sales in the long-term (one year), while 67 percent also cited exchange-rates as cause for concern in the short-term (three months), the survey showed.
These levels are barely changed from those borne out by a May DHL survey which showed 67 percent of UK exporters were most worried about sterling strength in both the short and long-term.

The pound last week leapt to 6-1/2 year highs against the German mark, propelled by broad weakness in the German currency and expectations of higher UK interest rates, but later fell back on profit taking.
However, the pound can still claim gains of about 25 percent, on a trade-weighted basis, since last August, forcing up exporters' prices along the way and forcing them to cut margins.
The latest Reuter foreign exchange poll found a consensus of market experts forecasting the pound would ease back to around 2.90 marks in three months time and 2.77 in a year's time.
Around forty percent of UK exporters cited raw material costs as their next greatest concern both short and long-term, down from forty-nine percent in May.

But while an increasing number of exporters said they would welcome British participation in the planned single currency, with 62 percent of exporters in favour of European economic and monetary union (EMU), 37 percent said economic and political tensions abroad would negatively affect their sales over the next three months.
Longer-term, however, export-confidence increased some five percent from May levels to 59 percent.
The DHL survey polled 1004 UK exporters.
